clock: the computer that ran the builder (UK time on Richard's PC)

rule.bands: A above 90%; B+ above 82.5% to 90%; B above 75% to 82.5%; C+ above 66.67% to 75%; C above 58.33% to 66.67%; C- above 50% to 58.33%; D above 25% to 50%; F up to 25%
rule.rank: percentile rank = (scores below + half the ties) / population size; the population of an item is every stock holding a score on that item from its registered run (or its published memo)
rule.registered_run: the newest live card in the conveyor's trays whose run holds scores; dry, cancelled and control runs never enter
rule.boundaries: per item, the lowest score that earned each grade today; null where no score earned that grade
rule.comparison_set: the stocks analysed by the new approach (the Sets of Questions/Items approach)
rule.fixed_letters: on memo topics 5, 6, 8, 11 and 12 a cell carrying fixed_letter shows the Rater's own letter from a real-world measure (A to F, no sub-grade), never re-cut; its rank and p are information only (D-SQ-267, D-SQ-271)
rule.fixed_cutoffs: v1.5 (his Messages 427 and 428; D-SQ-280): three letter rules, one per item, stated in each item's letter_rule. RANK within the population of stocks scored on the same scale (A top 10%; B next 15%, B+ its top half; C next 25% in thirds C+, C, C-; D next 25%; F bottom 25%) for the judgement items. His FIXED CUT-OFFS on the number (A 90 and above; B+ 82.5 to 89; B 75 to 82.4; C+ 66.67 to 74; C 58.33 to 66.66; C- 50 to 58.32; D 25 to 49; F below 25) for the items where 50 means neither positive nor negative: topics 1 and 2, Thesis's Change Forces' Strength, the External change forces and Internal change forces group judgements and their questions. The Rater's letter from his cut-offs on the MEASURE for topics 6, 8, 11 and 12, the number placed inside the letter's band. Rank and the percentile stay on every cell for information.
rule.scales: v1.5: every cell carries scale_tag; a rank letter is cut only among cells of the same scale (rater-v3 = the Rater v3.0 after the memo; rater-v2 and rater-v1-keyed = earlier Raters; writer-1.9 = the Investment Analyst's own score as it wrote the answer, the old method; writer-memo = the memo Analyst's own topic score). Old-method cells are labelled and stay until the Rater scores that stock's memo.
rule.scale_caveat: scores tagged rater-v1-keyed were set by the Rater of 1-Nov-26, whose key put 50 at the typical listed European company but was anchored on effect size rather than on percentiles; scores tagged rater-v2 or rater-v3 are standings in the Universe.

M:topic:1.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:1.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 46
M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: One strong, dated, law-backed tailwind (Dutch grid capex rising from about EUR 10bn to 18bn a year, permit-free substations from late 2027, the SF6 ban Alfen is already certified for) reaches only the grid unit, about 45% of revenue. It comes as volume only, rationed by the operators' technicians and permits (two of three installed 20-30% below plan in 2025), and three monopsony buyers hold its price. Against it, structural headwinds (cell makers selling turnkey, a renewed price war, VAT-rebate removal, charging prices in their seventh quarter of decline as value moves to site owners) act on the two units that make about 60% of gross profit. Consensus sales growth at the 80th percentile reflects the grid volume, but external forces give no support to group margin, so the net is slightly negative over two to three years: negative to mid-2027, mildly positive after. I am a touch above the External change forces group's 44 because the grid force is unusually well funded and dated.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:2.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 55
M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: Since October 2025 the outside chief executive has run a broad reset and met every dated milestone: three business units, headcount down from 1,053 to 909, EUR 13m of savings, working capital cut from EUR 159m to 58m, DC chargers exited and platforms rationalised, the CATL sodium-ion deal, and UK and Southern European launches. None of it has yet reached margin, EPS or guidance. The 2027 ambition has been cut to 'year-on-year improvement', this is the fourth finance director since January 2024, and the forecasts credit only about EUR 3m of net opex relief in FY27. I sit slightly above the group's 55 because the reset is far broader and better executed than a gentle drift, but the lagging outputs, the open finance seat and a repair rather than growth ambition keep it well short of a 75.

M:topic:5.reason: This scores the structure. Operating leverage is real and proven both ways: a 26-27% contribution margin on about EUR 100m of largely personnel opex, plus EUR 23-24m of fixed charges below EBITDA, so 10% more or less revenue moves EBITDA 40-50% (the same EUR 440m of revenue gave 18% EBITDA in FY22 and 5.9% in FY25). The other gears are absent or negative: prices fall in charging, follow cells in storage and are capped in grid; there is no financial leverage; the big cost-out is already in the base; and the feedback loops run mostly negative. Opex inflation also eats about a third of the drop-through, so the forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio from a near-zero base overstates the gearing. That is above the level-50 mix on gearing alone, but well short of Judges Scientific's 72-type proven leverage with stable pricing.

M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: The structural shift of Swedish savings to platforms is accelerating and is structural (share of savings capital 7.8% to 8.7%, 11.9% of market inflows, ISK threshold doubled, no inducement ban, the Riksbank turning from headwind to an asymmetric positive lever), and it supports 10-12% a year volume growth (consensus sales growth at the 85th percentile). Against it stand fast cyclical headwinds: trading activity normalising in a risk-off regime, a strong krona, competitors (Nordnet, SAVR, Montrose) taking yield at the margin, and the post-election bank-tax and ISK debate. That is a clear but partly offset net positive, a little above the groups' 53 because price and rates count as well as volume; between Linea Directa 63 and Instalco 58.

M:topic:1.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:1.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 62.0
M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: Two external legs reach most of sales: a broad Nordic construction turn still feeding 2027 revenue through the two-to-four-quarter lag (Swedish production +9% in 2026, starts +8%, Q2 intake +44%) and SEK 7-8bn of contracted data-centre work (about 10% of FY2027 revenue) with defence, transport and EPBD lengthening the tail; they are trimmed by margin headwinds (wages, copper, 15 bidders per tender, a second qualified data-centre bidder) and a rate turn that bites in 2028. Above Richard's 66 as he ruled (Swedish macro turning and data-centre build-outs) and coherent with the group's 70: more than Instalco's recovery alone, short of Helios Towers' structural, multi-year demand.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:2.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 50.0
M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: A completed, dated clean-up (Denmark from 0.1% to 5.1% and holding, the Swedish merger on budget with SEK 65m of savings, Finland's branch closures worth SEK 60-75m by FY2028, ABEKA sold, a rebuilt CFO/Sweden/M&A layer, the first buybacks) plus a genuinely new move into principal-contractor data-centre work, worth about 3-5% of EPS by FY2027 beyond what is in the base; offset by a stalled acquisition engine, 77% cash conversion, no internal audit and undated, never-met targets (the turnkey write-down risk is scored in topic 9). Above Richard's 48 and a little above the group's 57, because the data-centre capability is a large strategic move, but short of a full reset with growth on top.

M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:3.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 45.0
M:topic:3.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:3.reason: A defensible position without an economic moat: Nordic number two in a fragmented market (top five about 18%) where the tail sets price, with density, a 48% indexed service franchise (91% renewal) and rare complex-project capability, but gross margin stuck at 14-15% and EBITA at 5.2-6.9% for ten years (operating margin percentile 22) against peers at 7-8%; ROIC 12% (percentile 74) on capex under 1% of sales and 0.9x leverage is real, and the team is above median but has never delivered its margin target. Above Richard's 52 (not a poor business) and coherent with the groups' 54-60; beside MITIE (54) on its levels, above Vodafone but below Helios Towers' improving unit economics.

M:topic:4.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:4.reason: No short-term guidance; the undated 7% margin target has been missed for over ten years, the informal 'close to 7% in FY2026' has slipped to about 6.4% and all three operating targets were missed in FY2025, while volume beats in upswings (Q2 2026 EBITA +11% against consensus) are followed 12-18 months later by project-margin misses (2023, Q3 2025, FY2025 EPS consensus -5.8%); consensus now sits above every target and the company does nothing to steer it. Kept about 45 as Richard ruled and coherent with the groups' 42-44: slightly above Instalco, which missed every FY2025 target, below Sdiptech's newly set targets.

M:topic:5.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:5.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 38.0
M:topic:5.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:5.reason: About 90% of the cost base is variable (fixed costs 8-9%), price is nominal with a 9-12 month lag on unindexed Swedish contracts, financial leverage is trivial and cost-out is SEK 65m plus perhaps SEK 30-60m; the incremental margin of about 11% is idle capacity being refilled and fades to about 9% during 2027, and the data-centre reference loop is capped at two large projects. The model's EPS-to-revenue ratio of about 1.8x (FY2025-29 EPS +9.9% a year against revenue +5.5%) comes from savings, the Finnish fix, buybacks and a trough base, not from operating gearing, which resolves the contradiction Richard flagged: low gearing here and the same 90% variable costs narrowing the downside in topic 9; coherent with the Financial forecasts group (52) only on that reading.

M:topic:6.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:6.measure: Model adjusted EPS compound growth of about 9.9% a year over the four forecast years FY2025A to FY2029 (SEK 6.03 to 8.80); FY2026-30 gives about 7.1%
M:topic:6.letter_rule: fixed: the Rater's letter from Richard's cut-offs on the measure (never re-cut); the number sits inside the letter's band
M:topic:6.reason: The measure sits at the top of the 5-10% portion of C, but I place it in the middle of the band because the growth is a front-loaded, cycle-driven step (+17%, +14%, then +7% and +3%, consensus two-to-three-year EPS growth at the 5th percentile) and the margin path improves only about 70bp on a flat ten-year envelope without reaching 7%. It is organic plus about 1% a year of buybacks, with acquisitions at a trough, so the growth is honest but not compounding.

M:topic:1.reason: The external forces take from growth and margins over two to three years: beer about two-thirds of volume and structurally flat (footprint +0.3% a year, Western Europe -4% in H1 and Q3 2026), China volume -6% and -10% in the quarters that carry two-thirds of its profit with part of the loss share and channel, rule-driven mainstream price competition in the UK and Poland, dated regulation (Vietnamese excise, UK deposit scheme and sugar threshold) and a 2027 input-cost round of about 160bp of gross margin; the real external positives (soft drinks and alcohol-free growth, India, easy Chinese comparatives from Q2 2027, inflation-linked price pass-through in a rational oligopoly) only partly offset, and the PepsiCo licence wins and the Kazakhstan volume are the company's own and scored in topic 2. Consensus sales growth at the 31st percentile fits a clearly but not severely negative environment, just below Entra's mild negative and above Vodafone's, coherent with the External change forces group at 35.

M:topic:1.reason: The force that reaches the profit pool is structural and mandated: camera fitment from 49% to 60% of windscreens under EU GSR2, recalibration adding EUR 150-300 a job, a US claims-frequency recovery from 1.5% against a 2.1% average, the State Farm programme and a rising technical bar squeezing independents, plus PHE's ageing parc and TVH's recovery. Netted against it are the direct threats: US insurers starting to cap calibration and NAGS mark-ups, a mild El Nino winter, a weak US consumer, and a collapsing Belgian car market at Automotive, which falls from 17% to about 7% of profit. I sit above the group score of 56 because that score was anchored on flat group revenue, which is Automotive's shrinkage, while the profit-weighted balance is about 60/40 positive. That puts it a clear but offset positive, just above Linea Directa (a pricing cycle exposed to reversal) and below Eckert & Ziegler.

M:topic:5.reason: Several gears are proven at Belron. Calibration carries 80-90% incremental gross margin. Workshop density economics are steep, with incremental margin of 43-59%, and they cut both ways (2012: sales -4.4%, operating result -24%). Pricing power is real: NAGS-indexed pass-through, a 25% cash-pay premium, and price held while volume fell. Below the operating line, gearing and finance relief turn 1% of operating growth into 1.3-1.4% of PBT, there is EUR 45-55m of cost-out from mid-2027, and three reinforcing loops are at work. Together they turn about 3.4% revenue growth into about 11% EPS growth, about 3x against the Universe's 2x. It falls short of 90 because the financial leverage is junk-rated and 77% floating rather than comfortable, the insurer balancing loop is already fading incremental margins to 30%, and Automotive's 24% decremental gearing runs in reverse, so it sits above the economic-strength group's 50, which weighed the holding's drag rather than the structure.

M:topic:1.reason: Three external legs reach most of the business: the AI data-centre build (Data Center organic +44% in Q3, optical demand about 20% a year to 2031), the US private-fibre rebuild with BEAD orders landing from 2027 (North America 48% of sales, +80%), and defence. M:topic:1.reason: The Swedish building turn is now in installers' revenue (Instalco Sweden +15.2% organic in Q3, backlog +16.1%, Bravida Sweden +9%, starts +8%) with a dated public floor (defence, Norwegian hospitals, the Skanska schools framework) and pricing steadied by data centres absorbing rivals' technicians; but H2 organic rates are flattered by trough comparatives and halve from Q1 2027, the pricing relief is borrowed and reversible, Finland still contracts and a hiking Riksbank sets the 2027 demand slope. M:topic:1.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:1.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was None
M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: The 2026 lift came from forces that are reversing on a schedule: DSV's integration distraction (its recapture is planned over three to four quarters), Red Sea and Hormuz diversions holding yields up (Suez transits already at 58-59% of 2023), tariff front-loading, and a container delivery wave of 3.1m TEU in 2027 and 4.4m in 2028 against demand of about 4%. Those take unit gross profit down 4-5% a year, while lasting positives (customs complexity, technology and cloud demand, volume at or above the market) are smaller. Consensus sales growth at the 21st percentile and 3-year growth at the 4th agree. This is a scarcity price unwinding, but it hits a forwarder's yield, not a carrier's whole earnings, so the company sits well above Maersk; I am coherent with the group's 33.

A delivered, well-resourced repair that holds EBIT flat rather than growing it is a clear but partial positive, above Richard's 'gently positive but mediocre' CVS at 55 and in line with the group's 62.

M:topic:3.reason: The company is joint number one or two in sea and air and sits in the best, asset-light stage of a poor and fragmented value chain, protected by high barriers to the top tier, owned technology and some vertical switching costs. But it has a medium moat with no pricing power (it priced 6-12% below DSV in tenders), unit margins set outside the company, and a capable but conventional management with moderate targets. The figures (ROIC 18%, 88th percentile; ROE 93rd) are real, but growth is poor: EPS grew under 2% a year from 2019 to 2025, the business cannot reinvest at high returns, the Apex minority was bought at about CHF 3.6bn, and earnings swing hard with the cycle. So it is above Indutrade and below Linea Directa's structural cost advantage, coherent with the four groups (54, 54, 64, 53).

M:topic:1.reason: The external forces roughly cancel and tilt slightly negative over two to three years. The incumbents' price umbrella (market motor price +4% to 6%, non-life premiums +5.5% to 6%, Spanish GDP 2%+) lifts volume, but claims-cost growth of 3.5% to 4.5% (Baremo 3.3% to 3.5%, parts +5.1%), Mutua's open-ended tariff freeze, and Mapfre's and AXA's turn to volume from 2027 squeeze the 2027 margin and bring a soft-market risk forward to 2028. The 78th-percentile consensus sales growth is mostly price inflation, and the 2022 to 2023 loss shows how a severity step lands. This is a touch below the External change forces group's 50 because the soft-market threat now falls inside the window, and it sits between Kerry's neutral environment and Indutrade's soft backdrop.

The expense ratio fell from 22.1% to 19.4%, solvency was rebuilt to 191.5%, the dividend was restored and raised, guidance was raised twice in words and health moves to a new network in 2027. Consensus sales growth at the 86th percentile fits, but the force reaches the 40% prescription half, not the soft non-prescription 60% (9.4% against 10-12% guided), the per-pack fee help ends by mid-2027, and the co-payment rise invites a give-back contest with DocMorris and a low-probability political threat to the waiver. That is a strong leg that reaches only part of sales and is trimmed by fading price and a direct threat, so it sits at the 75 level, just under the group's 80, below Arteche and above RELX.

M:topic:1.reason: External forces are a clear, multi-part, structural net positive on the 88% of revenue outside Exhibitions: professionals using AI still need trusted data, so database owners keep customers and charge more at renewal (peers confirm it: Thomson Reuters Legal at 9-10%, Karnov AI tiers at +30%), law-firm IT spend doubled from 2% to 4% of revenue, STM demand rose from 4% to 6%, and falling model and token costs help margins. Against that sit a funded and direct threat at the Legal workflow layer (Harvey, Legora, Google), a cyclical Middle East dip in Exhibitions and small grant-rule and print drags; consensus sales growth at the 75th percentile is honest, but group organic growth is steady at about 7% rather than accelerating, so this is above Spie's favourable-but-mixed reading and below Helios Towers' broad structural pull, a touch above the 66 External change forces group because the forces reach nearly the whole perimeter.

M:topic:7.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:7.reason: Guidance, which counts most, will very likely be repeated in the same words; a verbal raise is unlikely because the wording is already at the top of its scale, and only the February buyback can surprise, in either direction. The memo puts consensus FY27 EPS at 60% held within 1.5%, with even odds of a 1.5-3% cut or raise and a mild upward drift by July from the margin beat and the lowest estimates catching up. That is an expected change of under 0.5% against 7% revenue growth, a ratio near 0.05 (about the 42nd percentile; EPS revisions are flat at the 45th). The narrative upgrade (that the second renewal holds) cannot arrive before late 2027, so this sits just below Kerry's modest upside with a stuck narrative and above Carlsberg's mixed picture, in line with the 52 group.

FY27 revisions have been 0% for six months, the share of Buy ratings fell seven points in a month, the guidance wording lost its double-digit Legal phrase, and the 200-day average has not risen in twelve months despite the price sitting 19% above it after a 13% three-month rise. M:topic:9.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:9.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was None
M:topic:9.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:9.reason: The fundamentals are simple and low-risk. Three drivers (sterling, margin delivery and Legal price at the second renewal, which falls outside the window), a constant-currency FY27 EPS cone of about -5% to +4% (plus or minus 3% for the dollar), low cyclicality with only Exhibitions' 12% cyclical, and leverage of about 2x with 82% of debt fixed, which is moderate rather than minimal. The share-price risk is high, sudden and poorly trackable: a 14.7% one-day fall on a competitor's launch, a beta of 1.2 to a de-rated peer group that explains half the variance, and half-yearly, rounded disclosure that hides a Legal slowdown until it lands. I score above the 58 first-layer Risks group and near the 70 third-and-fourth-layer group, below Imperial Brands' slow, predictable decline and above OEM International.

M:topic:10.reason: The memo's 'between turning up and early Broadening' is generous on the thesis and right on the price. The share price and multiple have turned up from a sentiment trough (+51% from the low, from 14.3x to about 18x), but the fundamentals are in steady mid-cycle Reinforcing: underlying growth flat at 7%, estimates unmoved for six months at the 45th percentile, Buy ratings falling, and the 200-day average not yet rising. Nothing is accelerating into growth, guidance or forecasts, and the catalysts ahead are confirmations rather than proofs. So the computed Broadening runs ahead of the evidence; this sits just below Kerry's mid-cycle Reinforcing and just above Banca Generali's late Reinforcing, with the turn in the multiple as what lifts it.

M:topic:4.reason: A deliberate beatable-floor style: 2023 met, 2025 beaten on growth and cash, 2026 raised twice from a guide set below consensus, and current FY2026 guidance implies only about 6% Q4 growth after a Q3 at 11.4%, so it is still a floor; management is visibly preparing a cautious FY2027 guide. M:topic:5.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:5.reason: Real structural operating gearing: 72% of opex is fixed, so 1% of volume adds about 3% to EBITA and 1% of price about 4%, proven both ways (+230bp of margin in 2019-22, -90bp in 2024), with cost-out of 15-20bp a year and financial leverage adding about 1.2x; but the pricing power is borrowed (price-over-opex spread -19bp in 2025, about -7bp in 2027), the up-slope is only 5-7bp per point against 15-40bp on the way down, and the forecast EPS-to-revenue growth ratio of about 1.9x is the Universe's median. Large leverage in the structure that disappoints on the way up, so the upper part of the 50 level, above the Economic strength group (45).

M:topic:9.reason: The 2027 EPS cone of 2.42-3.36 euros around 2.97 (-19%/+13%) is skewed down, the drivers (copper, hyperscaler capex, GCG) are correlated through the AI-and-electrification trade, operating leverage is three to four times steeper on the way down, and the share price carries sudden French-spread and sentiment events; against that the case rests on few drivers observable within one reporting cycle, FCF is countercyclical (700-780m euros in every scenario) and leverage stays below 2.3x against a 3.5x covenant. M:topic:1.reason: Defence (47% of FY26 revenue) gets a funded, structural UK and NATO budget rise, and the 20/40/40 doctrine points it at Steatite's and Custom Power's products. The industrial destock has ended, and AI data-centre and US autonomy demand add a small third leg. These are offset by direct threats that are certain sooner: DRAM and component inflation, a £28bn Treasury funding gap with CMA screening that lengthens awards, the US continuing resolution, and unhedged dollar purchasing. I put it above the External change forces group (63) because this is a clear multi-part positive reaching most of sales, but below a 75 because the restock is a pulse and the defence money turns into contracts on a contested calendar.

M:topic:3.reason: Accreditation and design-in give a genuine but narrow moat on about 60% of revenue (Systems and Power). M:topic:5.reason: Operating leverage is large and proven both ways. A £42m fixed overhead on a 33.5% gross margin puts break-even at about £110m to £115m; FY25's 23% revenue fall cut operating profit 65%, and each £10m of Systems revenue now adds about £3m of operating profit. Part of the gain is given back by the company's own choices: the ORNANE refinancing adds 2% to the share count and about EUR 30m of interest, so EPS lags EBITA by 2 to 3 points a year, and the new project-heavy segments have had overruns. That is more ambition than Richard's 'gently positive but mediocre' CVS (55) and close to OEM International's (66) turn into an active acquirer, but the dilution keeps it below that. I sit slightly above the group's 57 because the size of the acquisition step-up is itself a large change force.

M:topic:3.reason: The qualitative parts are good but not exceptional. Germany is a fragmented market that SPIE consolidates and France is a rational oligopoly where SPIE is only number four. Moderate, mostly widening advantages come from prequalified grid and nuclear crews, a recruiting edge, frameworks with retention above 90%, and -34 days of working capital that funds growth. Management is disciplined but risk-averse, with organic growth averaging 1.8%. The Universe figures understate the financial profile: gross margin (pct 6), EBITDA margin (pct 19) and ROIC of 4.1% (pct 30) reflect a labour-services model and EUR 4.4bn of goodwill. Cash conversion (pct 93), returns on tangible capital above 50% and margins at the top of the peer group are the truer reading, though Deutsche Bank's 9.1% return on cumulative acquisition spend is only about the cost of capital and 56% of costs go to subcontracting. I place it in line with the groups (55 to 63), a little above the comparable MITIE (54) and just below Linea Directa (64).

M:topic:5.reason: Structurally this is contribution-margin leverage, not fixed-cost leverage. Only about 4-5% of revenue is truly fixed overhead, the incremental margin is 11-12% against a 7.8% average, so 1% more revenue gives about 1.5% more EBITA. Pass-through pricing is proven (the margin rose from about 5% to 7.6% through 4-6% wage inflation), but real price is worth only 5-10 bps a year. There is little cost scope by design. Financial leverage is modest and moving against EPS (EBITA converts to EPS at about 0.85x in FY2026-FY2027), and the acquisition loop still reinforces but buys less each year. The forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio is only about 1.2x against a Universe median near 2x. It sits a little above the low-gearing services peers Bravida (36) and MITIE (38) on the strength of proven pass-through and the self-funding loop, and below the group's 55, which leans on cash conversion rather than gearing.

M:topic:12.measure: The memo's central return at its fair 12-13x multiple is about -5% to 0% to December 2027; weighting its scenarios (bull 30% at about +20%, base 50%, bear 15%, severe 5%) gives about -1% over 18 months
M:topic:12.letter_rule: fixed: the Rater's letter from Richard's cut-offs on the measure (never re-cut); the number sits inside the letter's band
M:topic:12.reason: A small weighted loss gives F, and about -1% maps to about 24. I move it down one for the fat lower tail (a fair trough 35-45% below the price on a tariff reversal). The near-term +5-10% over six to nine months and the three-year check of +3% to +9% keep it at the top of the band.

M:master:setups_fit.because: Rating = 50 (standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies), set by the Rater. The best fit is a Demand-driven EPS Upgrader, but the step-up is mostly a policy-and-refill price rent rather than a durable demand shift. Only deepwater, a fifth of sales, is structural demand, and the earnings step reverses from 2028. The case therefore fits the setup in kind while missing its key element of durable demand. I score the fit in substance only and leave the top-of-range multiple to topics 11 and 12, which is why it sits at 50, in line with the memo's C.

M:topic:1.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 62.0
M:topic:1.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:1.reason: On the business that stays (Vision and Machinery from mid-2027) the external picture is a mild net positive: a real Vision upturn (order book EUR 170m from EUR 126m, APAC semis, Jenoptik and Basler raising, PMI 52.9) fading toward mid-single digits, and a tyre-maker capex freeze (Machinery book -38%, Goodyear capex cut) that is deferral of a replacement-led wave expected to turn late 2027, trimmed by Chinese 2D vision pricing. The strong grid and offshore legs that lift the group figure (External change forces group 60) leave with Electrification, so I score below the group, just below OEM International's modest positive and above Kerry's neutral.

M:topic:2.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)
M:topic:2.note: set by the Rater; the Investment Analyst's own score was 72.0
M:topic:2.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:2.reason: The most complete reset in TKH's history, largely delivered on time: separation approved with 100% of votes, non-core disposals closed, nine vision brands cut to two, the EUR 200m capex done and Eemshaven repaired, leverage 2.6x to 1.8x, an external CEO from January, and proceeds of about EUR 950m (half the market cap) to turn debt into net cash and fund the buyback. It sits below a 77 because the payoff still needs one transaction and an untaken capital-return decision, and it is net of present problems (18.3% working capital, 15% H1 cash conversion, 51.6% of research capitalised, an audit key matter, the STAK structure); coherent with the Internal change forces group at 72.

M:topic:3.scale_version: the Rater v3.0, 2026-11-03: standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10), every item scored after the memo is written, the case first on judgement topics, anchors from the corrected ordering of 75 companies, the question groups' keys (D-SQ-280)

M:topic:3.letter_rule: rank within this item's population of the same scale (A top 10%, B next 15%, C, D and F quarters; B+, B, C+, C, C- sub-grades)
M:topic:3.reason: Judged as it is becoming: one real fortress (VMI, over 70% of outsourced radial tyre-building machines, homologation barriers, price held through a 38% backlog fall) and a defensible 3D vision niche, beside commoditising 2D vision, 5% research intensity against 13-14% at peers, a weak and changing management (Management group 36) and a bolt-on vision strategy where its integration record is worst. The continuing financial profile (27% pro forma ROCE, 18% margin, net cash) is better than the reported figures (ROIC 6.4%, p47; EBITDA margin p23), but Machinery is cyclical and the earnings base needs four corrections, so the business is mid-quality and only a little above typical, between Helios Towers and Vodafone.

M:topic:5.reason: The group's high, proven operating leverage (about 50% drop-through; H1 2026 revenue +11.4%, EBITA +41.7%) belongs mostly to Eemshaven's absorption, and that leaves with the sale. M:topic:9.reason: The mechanism is simple, but the case is a sequential chain (sale, proceeds, buyback, EPS, re-rating) whose risks multiply. It rests on two external events management does not control: a sale price in a hostile financing regime (25-35% odds of a slip) and the untrackable timing of tyre-maker capex. Four un-guided variables sit between segment profit and EPS, FY2027 EPS has two non-overlapping branches, and the 18-month price cone runs from EUR 36-40 to EUR 72-78, with 35-45% downside to a trough multiple. Operations (about plus or minus 8% on EBITA), dated catalysts and the move to net cash keep it above the most complex conglomerates, coherent with the Risks groups at 44 and 36.
